listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, November 18. Our lead story is Nvidia. The chip company reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday. That was after the dramatic exit of chief executive Jensen Huang. The board says it does not intend to reinstate him. Huang has said he would be honored to return if the board allowed it. In China, there is worry that the scandal could raise pressure on the United States to restrict advanced chip sales further. Now to other front page stories. Mary Peltola has narrowly won Alaska's Senate race, according to an Associated Press race call. She defeated the Republican incumbent, and the seat moves to the Democrats. Vladimir Putin will meet President Trump and Chinese President Xi on Wednesday. This comes after a Ukrainian attack partially collapsed a bridge that Russia prizes. In the Gulf, Iran fired drones at a US radar facility in Bahrain. It was the third round of strikes. The United States fired at Iranian targets along a shipping route. In tech, OpenAI introduced GPT six point two Astra, its new frontier model, and GPT six point two Sol, a more efficient model for everyday work. Now the sections. In Tech and AI, Simon Willison is exploring external sandboxes for coding agents. Claude Platform also added Linked billing in beta, so your customers can pay for usage through their own Claude organization. In Politics, The Lever reports the White House is bypassing normal procedure to install Eric Ueland as a government watchdog for fifteen years. In World news, Secretary of State Marco Rubio says there is zero information that United States outages were caused by a malign actor. In Sports, the Houston Rockets, eleven and four, visit the Indiana Pacers. Olson won a Silver Slugger Award after hitting forty one homers. In Atlanta, the owner of Underground Atlanta has bought an iconic John Portman tower on Peachtree Street. The Board of Regents also named Timothy Lieuwen as sole finalist to lead Georgia Tech. In Architecture, Ricoh launched a tougher three hundred sixty degree camera for construction sites. In Science and Nature, NASA's NICER telescope has ended science operations after six and a half years beyond its initial mission. The scimitar-horned oryx is also back in Chad. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as it reports soaring sales
lead.note: Nvidia reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday, the first results since the dramatic exit of chief executive Jensen Huang. The company also said it will not reinstate him. NPR reports that Huang said he would be honored to return if the board allowed it, but the board says it has no intention of doing so. Silicon Valley leaders have pushed for his return. The episode reaches beyond one company. BBC reports that China worries the scandal could raise pressure on the United States to restrict sales of advanced chips further. The Lever raises fresh questions about lawmakers' investments in tech companies they regulate, as Nvidia's stock sinks. For a reader who follows AI closely, the story links the chip supply behind the industry with leadership turmoil, politics and US-China relations, all in the same week.
